name: Average hourly earnings after inflation
definition: Average hourly earnings of all private-sector employees on New York City payrolls, annual average, in 2025 dollars (deflated with the New York-area consumer price index).

latest_extra.note: Monthly figure in current (nominal) dollars, not adjusted for inflation and not seasonally adjusted, so it is not directly comparable to the 2025-dollar annual series. Preliminary.

source.name: Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Employment Statistics (State and Metro Area), New York City, total private, average hourly earnings of all employees, not seasonally adjusted, series SMU36935610500000003

deflator_source.name: Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U), New York-Newark-Jersey City, all items, not seasonally adjusted, series CUURS12ASA0

method: AHE_y = mean of the 12 monthly CES average-hourly-earnings values for year y. CPI_y = mean of the monthly CPI-U values (CUURS12ASA0) for year y. Real value in 2025 dollars = AHE_y x CPI_2025 / CPI_y, rounded to cents. CPI_2025 = 345.511 (mean of 11 months). The series starts in 2007, the first year CES published this earnings series for New York City.
caveats: BLS published no October 2025 value for the New York-area CPI (data collection lapsed during the October-November 2025 federal shutdown), so CPI_2025 is the mean of the 11 published months.
An average across all private jobs: it rises when low-wage jobs disappear (as in 2020) even if no one's pay went up, so read it alongside the jobs count.
Covers jobs located in the city, whoever holds them; government workers are excluded.
Peers left out: CES earnings series at the city level exist for New York City but not for most peer cities.
